result.rule: Use an exclusive merge for alternative paths; it does not wait for inactive alternatives.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Build a connected path from each modeled start to an end or intentionally continuing state. Avoid accidental disconnected flow nodes.
Trace every split to continuations or endings. Add a join only when paths reunite and choose matching waiting semantics.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.

result.rule: When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives or says an activity may or may not occur, and the paths later continue in common: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway, and reconnect the alternative paths with an exclusive merge before their shared continuation.

When the description states that an item is received by a specific role after a preceding activity: Model the receipt as a distinct activity assigned to the receiving role, preserving its stated sequence; do not use a generic receipt activity that omits the recipient.

When the description identifies mutually exclusive destinations for an item or output: Model each destination as a distinct activity on an exclusive branch, then merge the branches before their shared continuation.

When the description distinguishes an initial submission or initiation from a subsequent registration of the item before another activity: Model the submission and the subsequent registration as separate activities, preserving their stated order and dependency.

trace.reason: Check whether a documented guideline already covers faithful activity labeling or forbids this modeling instruction.

result.rule: Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.

args.text: When labeling a BPMN activity, preserve the action and actor stated in the process description; avoid replacing them with a related but distinct action or omitting a meaningful actor.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already captures the label-faithfulness issue.

result.rule: When the description states an activity, its object, scope, or recipient: Label the corresponding BPMN element so that it preserves the described action, object, scope, and direction; do not replace them with a related action or add unsupported details.

When the description states a specific activity or process-ending outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or end event with a concise phrase that preserves the stated action or outcome; do not substitute a related action or add an unsupported one.

When the description states an action from the perspective of the person or participant receiving a service, item, or information: Label the BPMN activity to preserve the direction and perspective stated in the description; do not recast it as the corresponding sender-side action.

When the description states an activity together with criteria, optional supporting actions, or a later outcome associated with it: Label the BPMN task with a concise verb-object phrase for the activity itself. Keep associated criteria, alternatives, and subsequent outcomes out of the label unless they define the activity.
